matt: Hey support — customer running traffic through a bastion+NAT to our VPCE is seeing intermittent 502s for /v1/generate. Works from the internet but fails from their app stack after cutover. Any quick checks?

lina: Do they have Private DNS enabled on the interface endpoint? Could be split-horizon resolving api.redwood.com -> vpce IP.

matt: They said yes. Error from client sometimes shows `tls: handshake failure` and our LB logs a 502. Sample curl they ran: ```curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.com/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"```

ashley: That smells like a transparent proxy / TLS bump on the bastion intercepting 443 and presenting its own cert. Can they hit the VPCE IP directly from a host that routes the same path and inspect the cert? Also check if traffic is being hairpinned to the NATGW instead of going to the interface endpoint ENI.

matt: Route table shows 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw, but they added a specific route for the VPCE CIDR to local. The bastion runs a squid proxy configured to intercept outbound 443 (iptables redirect). If squid intercepts, it can rewrite SNI/cert.

ben: Ask them to run these repro steps and attach outputs:
1) `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts`
2) `curl -v --trace-ascii - --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.com/v1/health` (inspect Server certificate CN + SNI)
3) `sudo tcpdump -nn -s0 -w /tmp/vpce-443.pcap host 10.0.5.12 and port 443` and share the pcap.

infra-bot: route-update job applied for account-123 at 2026-03-10T12:05Z :information_source:

ashley: In a similar customer case the transparent proxy did TLS bump and did not exclude the interface endpoint CIDR, causing SNI/cert mismatch and intermittent 502s (some flows used NAT, some used direct ENI). Fix was to bypass proxy for VPCE prefixes or stop transparent interception for destinations inside the VPC. Also verify source/dest check on the bastion ENI and that the bastion is not SNATting traffic destined for the VPCE back out via the NATGW.

matt: Requested they add an ACL to bypass squid for the VPCE CIDR and disable iptables redirect for that range. They applied the change and reported calls now return 200 consistently. Will monitor for 24h. Thanks all :thumbsup:
